name: Hire trades through the union hall
summary: When a self-perform crew needs another carpenter, finisher or labourer, the general foreman either asks a member he knows by name or calls the union hall, which dispatches the next qualified member from its out-of-work list with a referral slip. HR then collects the tax and banking forms and checks the working at heights and WHMIS certificates before the worker is set up for payroll and sent to site orientation. Hires are fast when the hall has members free, but in the spring ramp-up some trades run short, workers turn up without current training, and some never show, so crews start short-handed.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national general contractor bound to ICI building trades agreements, hiring about 140 hourly trades a month into self-perform concrete, carpentry and labour crews.
baseline.notes: One case is one hourly hire from the crew hire request to the worker reaching site orientation. Recalls of recently laid-off workers are in hr-layoff-recall.

trigger: The weekly crew plan asks for more workers of a trade on a project.
end_state: The worker has a referral slip, verified certificates and an employee record, and is at site orientation; or the request is refilled after a no-show.

volume.seasonality: Hiring peaks from April to June and slows from November to February.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate: field workforce of 1,050 to 1,700 with project-based layoffs and rehiring.
Matches the organisation file; the field workforce grows by about 650 workers between winter and summer.
About 45 minutes of calls and coordination per hire x 140 hires.
About 70 minutes of paperwork per hire.
Approvals to hire from other sources.
Outside hires only.
Course bookings for missing certificates.
Receiving new hires at the gate.
Paid travel on the first day, standing for all new hires of any trade.

systems.name: Safety management system (hazard assessments, inspections, incidents, training records)

steps.name: Receive the crew hire request
steps.description: The general foreman takes the hire request from the weekly crew plan: trade and classification, number of workers, site, start date and any tickets the work needs (working at heights, forklift, swing stage). He writes it on his hiring list for the week.

error.defect_description: Wrong classification or ticket requirement noted.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the request comes from spe-crew-planning.

steps.name: Decide between a name request and hall dispatch
steps.description: The general foreman checks whether he knows a good member of the local who is out of work (from his own phone list or word on site) and whether the agreement's name-request share is still open on this project. Recalls of workers laid off in the last few weeks go through the layoff and recall process instead.

error.defect_description: Name-request share exceeded on a project.

control.basis: Collective agreement hiring clause: hire through the Local Union office; a set share of hires may be requested by name (BACU-Guild ICI art. 5.01, 5.03)

next.condition: known member to request by name

evidence.note: Art. 5.03 lets 75% of hires be requested by name; route shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Phone the named member
steps.description: The general foreman calls the member, describes the site, start date and expected length of the job, and checks the member is free and has current working at heights and WHMIS cards.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Call the union hall for dispatch
steps.description: The general foreman phones the local's dispatcher with the job location, type of work, classification, agreement, start date and any special skills or tickets, and the dispatcher logs the request.

error.defect_description: Ticket requirement not passed to the hall.

evidence.note: Rule 2.15: the dispatcher records job location, type of work, classification and agreement.

steps.name: Register the name request with the local
steps.description: The general foreman, or HR for larger requests, tells the local office which member is being hired by name so the hall can check the member's standing and the project's name-request share and issue the referral slip.

control.basis: Collective agreement and union hiring rules: name hires need a referral or clearance slip before starting work (LIUNA Local 183 Rule 2.12; BACU-Guild ICI art. 5.01)

steps.name: Union hall dispatches from the out-of-work list
steps.description: The dispatcher calls members on the out-of-work list in order of registration who have the skills and tickets asked for, between noon and 5 p.m., until one accepts. In the spring ramp-up the list for some trades runs short.

error.defect_description: Member dispatched without a required ticket.

evidence.note: Rules 2.16-2.17 describe dispatch order and call hours; wait and shortfall share are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Labour relations approves hiring from other sources
steps.description: When the local confirms it cannot supply qualified members in time, the labour relations manager checks the agreement and the union's confirmation, and approves hiring a non-member who must apply for probationary membership before starting.

control.basis: Collective agreement: employer may hire from other sources as probationary members when the union cannot supply (BACU-Guild ICI art. 5.05)

steps.name: Recruit a candidate from other sources
steps.description: The recruiter posts the opening on job boards, calls referrals from foremen and screens candidates by phone for experience and tickets, then sends the chosen candidate to the local to sign up as a probationary member.

next.condition: candidate signs up with the local

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Local issues the referral slip
steps.description: The local office checks the member is in good standing (or signs up the probationary member) and issues a referral or clearance slip naming the employer and project, which the worker brings on the first day.

evidence.note: LIUNA Rule 2.03 and BACU art. 5.01; wait is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Send the new-hire packet
steps.description: The HR administrator emails the worker the new-hire packet: federal and provincial TD1 forms, direct deposit form, emergency contact, personal information form and the list of certificates to bring.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common onboarding paperwork.

steps.name: Worker returns the forms and certificates
steps.description: The worker fills in the forms and sends photos of the referral slip, working at heights card, WHMIS certificate and any trade certificates, often from a phone, or brings them to the yard office.

error.defect_description: Form incomplete or a certificate missing or expired.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Check documents and training certificates
steps.description: The HR administrator checks that the forms are complete, the referral slip names the right project and classification, and the working at heights and WHMIS certificates are current and from approved providers, and records them in the HRIS training record.

control.basis: Ontario OHSA and O. Reg. 297/13: workers who use fall protection on construction projects must have approved working at heights training, and employers keep the training record

evidence.note: IHSA: every worker should have working at heights and WHMIS training; unions refer only trained members (BACU art. 7.03); share missing is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Book the worker on a working at heights course
steps.description: The safety training coordinator books the worker on the next approved working at heights or WHMIS course, usually a one-day class, and sends the date; the start date moves back until the certificate is in hand.

control.basis: Working at heights training before work at heights (O. Reg. 297/13)

evidence.note: Wait for course seats is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Create the employee record and pass it to payroll
steps.description: The HR administrator creates the employee in the HRIS with union local, classification, rate group, province, site and start date, and sends the packet to payroll for set-up before the next timecard batch.

error.defect_description: Wrong local or classification gives the wrong rate and dues.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Confirm the start and assign the crew
steps.description: The general foreman phones the worker to confirm the start date, time and gate, tells the foreman whose crew he joins, and checks PPE sizes and tools the worker must bring.

next.condition: worker takes another job or does not answer

evidence.note: Author's estimate of drop-outs between referral and start.

steps.name: New hire travels to the site
steps.description: On the first morning the new worker drives to the project; travel time and kilometres are paid when the site is outside the free travel zone of his local.

evidence.note: Travel expense and travel time rules (art. 17, 18.06); the wait to the start date and the trip length are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Foreman receives the worker at the gate
steps.description: The foreman meets the worker at the site gate, checks the referral slip and PPE, and waits for the owner's or the site's access badge on secured sites such as hospitals before walking him to the site orientation.

control.basis: Site entry rules: PPE and site orientation before starting work (OHSA s. 25(2)(a))

evidence.note: Employer duty to provide information and instruction; access waits on secured sites are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Hand the worker to site orientation
steps.description: The foreman hands the worker to the site safety coordinator for the site-specific orientation, which is recorded under the safety training process, and the worker joins the crew after it.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Record the hire and update the ratio tracker
steps.description: The HR administrator closes the hire on the hiring list, records whether it was a name request, dispatch or outside hire for the project's name-request ratio, and files the referral slip in the employee file.

error.defect_description: Hire not counted in the ratio.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Hall cannot supply
exceptions.description: The local cannot supply qualified members in time and a probationary member is recruited from other sources.

exceptions.name: Training missing or expired
exceptions.description: The worker is booked on a working at heights or WHMIS course before starting.

exceptions.name: No-show or drop-out
exceptions.description: The worker takes another job or does not arrive and the hall is called again.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from hire request to the worker at site orientation
benchmarks.population: ICI union hiring by a large general contractor

evidence.note: Author's estimate: dispatch usually the same or next day (calls between noon and 5 p.m., LIUNA Rule 2.17), paperwork one to two days, start on the next working morning, with a weekend in about a third of cases; longer when training or outside hiring is needed.

pain_points.description: In the spring ramp-up the out-of-work list for some trades runs short, so crews start short-handed while the hall searches or the company recruits outside.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Workers arrive without current working at heights or WHMIS certificates and lose days waiting for a course seat.
Paper forms collected by phone photo are often incomplete, delaying payroll set-up for the first payday.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

sources.title: BACU-Guild Province Wide ICI Collective Agreement (marble, tile, terrazzo, cement masons, resilient floor layers and helpers), 1 April 2022 to 30 April 2025
sources.publisher: Brick and Allied Craft Union of Canada and Terrazzo, Tile & Marble Guild of Ontario; filed with Employment and Social Development Canada (Negotech)
sources.supports: Art. 5.01 employer hires from the Local Union office and the union supplies a referral slip; 5.02 recall within 35 days of layoff; 5.03 75% of additional hires may be requested by name; 5.05 hire from other sources as probationary members when the union cannot supply; 7.03 union refers only members with Fall Arrest, WHMIS and Working at Heights training; 18.03 deductions and contributions compiled monthly and remitted with the report form by the 15th of the following month; 18.04 three remittance forms each month; 19.01 5% a month liquidated damages on remittances more than 10 days in arrears; 22.01 timesheets mandatory, paper sheets due by end of business day Monday after the workweek; 22.02 time books closed weekly and Thursday payday within four working days of closing; 22.03 direct deposit by 5 p.m. Thursday; 22.04 pay statement contents; 22.05 two hours' pay per day of late pay; 24.01 normal week of four or five days of 8 to 10 hours.

sources.title: Hiring Hall and Clearance Rules
sources.publisher: Labourers' International Union of North America (LIUNA) Local 183
sources.supports: All hiring through the union office and every person dispatched holds a referral slip (Rule 2.03); on an employer call the dispatcher records job location, type of work, classification and agreement (2.15); referral in order of registration with calls between 12 and 5 p.m. (2.16-2.17); name hires and recalls per the collective agreement, with a referral or clearance slip before starting (2.12); members certify OHSA, WHMIS and Working at Heights training (2.05, 3.04); penalty for failing to report or quitting within five days (2.21).

sources.title: Getting Started
sources.supports: Every construction worker should receive working at heights and WHMIS training; employers must give workers information, instruction and supervision (OHSA s. 25(2)(a)); further training depends on the work and hazards.

assumptions: Name requests are 60% of hires, hall dispatch 40%, within the 75% name-request share some agreements allow.
Recalls within the agreement's recall window are handled in hr-layoff-recall and are not counted here.
Site-specific orientation is the next process (hse-safety-training) and is not timed here.
The labourer role stands for any new hire's paid first-day travel.
The organisation file lists hr-admin, general-foreman and labour-relations-manager; recruiter, safety-trainer and foreman are added because they do steps.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file.

The simulated median (about 6 days) is above the 5-day estimate because the triangular waits for dispatch and forms have long tails and 28% of cases loop back (missing training, incomplete forms, no-shows); both are author estimates and the gap is within the expected range.
